He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. Green was part of the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian basketball team]] that won bronze at the [[2020 Tokyo Olympics]].{{cite web|title=Basketball GREEN Josh|url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/basketball/athlete-profile-n1326472-green-josh.htm|work=[[Tokyo 2020 Olympics]]|access-date=10 October 2021|language=en-us|archive-date=10 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211010224657/https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/basketball/athlete-profile-n1326472-green-josh.htm|url-status=dead}} He was also part of the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian basketball team]] at the [[2024 Paris Olympics]]. {{Cite web |date=2024-09-18 |title=Australia Team Profile - Men's Olympic Basketball Tournament Paris 2024 {{!}} FIBA Basketball |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/teams/australia |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}} ==Early life== Green was born in [[Sydney]] to Australian mother Cahla and American-born father Delmas. His parents met while both were playing semi-professional basketball in Australia.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/25794761|title=Josh Green is an Australian first, basketball player second |publisher=ESPN |access-date=25 March 2023|date=21 January 2019}} The couple decided to raise a family in the north-west Sydney suburb of [[Castle Hill, New South Wales|Castle Hill]] where Josh began playing basketball at the age of five when his mother started coaching him. Along with playing local basketball for the [[Hills Hornets]] as a child, Green tried an array of sports as a junior and excelled in [[Australian rules football]], [[Sport of athletics|athletics]], basketball, [[Rugby football|rugby]], [[association football|soccer]] and [[swimming (sport)|swimming]]. Green currently holds the world record for 7 year olds in the 500m with a time of 1:29:50.{{Cite web |title=INTERNATIONAL AGE RECORDS |url=https://trackinfo.org/SingleAgeRecords.html |access-date=2024-11-01 |website=trackinfo.org}} By the age of 10, he had been selected to represent his home state of [[New South Wales]] in nine separate sports.{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2798917-preps-hoops-star-josh-green-is-ready-to-take-his-next-step |title=Preps star Josh Green ready to commit |publisher=Bleacher Report |date=5 October 2018}} In fifth grade, Green traveled more than 12 hours by car to the [[outback]] town of [[Broken Hill, New South Wales|Broken Hill]] in an attempt to gain selection for the under-12 state basketball team and was told he was good enough to be on the team but would have to wait a year or two so the older boys could play. Twelve months later, he captained the under-12 NSW Metro state team to a national title. Green switched to play club basketball for Penrith in 2013 and the decision paid off when he was selected to represent the under-14 and under-16 New South Wales state teams in successive years as a bottom-ager.{{cite web |url=https://westernweekender.com.au/2020/04/josh-green-on-verge-of-nba-dream-becoming-reality/ |title=Josh Green on verge of NBA dream becoming reality |publisher=The Western Weekender |date=16 April 2020}} Green was also a prodigious [[Australian rules football]]er in his younger years{{cite web |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/basketball/ben-simmons-has-already-taken-high-school-basketball-star-josh-green-under-his-wing/news-story/3aff201301a79818709136f25b1a68e2 |title=Ben Simmons has already taken high school basketball star Josh Green under his wing |publisher=News.com.au |date=31 January 2019}}{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R6MTeMvbwDE |title=Arizona Wildcats' Josh Green – Australia's Next Basketball Star |publisher=Trans World Sport |date=26 February 2018}}{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=llxPus2AtwU |title=Josh Green Nike Hoop Summit Interview |publisher=Draft Express |date=18 April 2018}} while playing locally for the Westbrook Bulldogs and would regularly attend [[Sydney Swans]] home games with his father. Green claims to have "loved" playing Australian rules football{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/a-weekend-with-josh-green-australias-next-sporting-superstar/news-story/6b2edff6900af7f17dab4c28420e02b8 |title=A weekend with Josh Green, Australia's next sporting superstar |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=8 March 2019}}{{cite web |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/josh-green-pumped-to-represent-australia-on-the-hardwood-in/article_cd1c4d05-f236-5555-9c89-62221caf7ba6.html |title=Josh Green pumped to represent Australia on the hardwood in Hoop Summit game |work=Arizona Daily Star |date=11 April 2019}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/26801651 |title=Josh Green: Australia's latest basketball star headed for Arizona |publisher=ESPN Australia |access-date=25 March 2023|date=24 May 2019}} and has "always been a big Swans fan", naming [[Adam Goodes]] and [[Lance Franklin]] as his favourite players growing up.{{cite web |url=https://wwos.nine.com.au/basketball/basketball-josh-green-reacts-to-comparisons-to-australian-nba-star-ben-simmons/b3b17277-225f-42d5-950d-f9885d29e997 |title=Rising Australian basketball star and 'freak athlete' Josh Green on track for bright NBA future |publisher=Wide World of Sports |date=8 February 2019}} Such was his talent in Australian rules football, the Swans and fellow professional football club [[Greater Western Sydney Giants]] offered him a place in their junior developmental academies. At the age of 13, Green accepted an offer to join the Giants' academy.{{cite web |url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/basketball/josh-green-becomes-first-australian-since-ben-simmons-to-be-mcdonalds-allamerican/news-story/9755d636f4a00bbc40c7e86847b5df3a |title=Josh Green becomes first Australian since Ben Simmons to be McDonald's All-American |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=25 January 2019}}{{subscription rules football{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SGpvDZNcAL8 |title=5 Star Arizona Commit Josh Green Q+A |publisher=BallerVisions |date=23 December 2018}} after the family relocated to Mountain Ridge with title hopes |publisher=AZ Central |date=28 December 2015}} ==High school career== While in [[Sydney]], Green attended [[The King's School, Parramatta|The King's School]] in Parramatta and dominated the local basketball scene so much that he was selected to represent the New South Wales' under 16 state team at the age of 13.{{cite web |url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/newslocal/west/sport/four-youngsters-from-penrith-basketball-selected-into-nsw-under16-state-teams/news-story/8586d588e9c585c53171b18c3e568e00 |title=Four youngsters from Penrith Basketball selected into NSW under-16 State teams |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=29 May 2014}}{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/meet-josh-green-the-australian-taking-over-the-american-high-school-basketball-scene/news-story/e168bdba13cbb0ff848dccb3bf045179 |title=Meet Josh Green, the Australian taking over the American high school basketball scene |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=29 September 2017}} Later that year, the Green family relocated to [[Phoenix, Arizona]], and in 2015, Josh enrolled at [[Mountain Ridge High School (Arizona)|Mountain Ridge High School]], where he impressed.[https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/12/28/green-brothers-lift-mountain-ridge-title-hopes/77982208/ Green brothers lift Mountain Ridge with title hopes] In 2017, he transferred to the [[IMG Academy]] in Florida and became a five-star draft prospect.{{cite web |url=http://www.couriermail.com.au/sport/more-sports/josh-green-has-been-rated-a-fivestar-recruit-as-us-colleges-continue-to-fight-for-him/news-story/ee70c4f89019efd72c05374077949a41 |title=Josh Green has been rated a five-star recruit, as US colleges continue to fight for him |work=Courier Mail |date=11 January 2018}} In the final game of his high school career, Green led IMG to a national championship victory with a 65–55 win over [[La Lumiere School|La Lumiere]] and was subsequently named MVP of the championship game.{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/australias-josh-green-leads-img-academy-to-geico-nationals-championship/news-story/074bbabbff7706f4101a9ae041eee254 |title=Australia's Josh Green leads IMG Academy to GEICO Nationals Championship |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=7 April 2019}} He was selected for the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], along with fellow UA recruit [[Nico Mannion]].{{cite web |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-wildcats-signees-nico-mannion-josh-green-named-to-mcdonald/article_9e582720-2016-11e9-9e1b-d32d50376ff2.html |title=Arizona Wildcats signees Nico Mannion, Josh Green named to McDonald's All-American Game |work=Arizona Daily Star |date=24 January 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Green received an offer to join the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]] in April 2018.{{cite web |url=https://www.vuhoops.com/2018/4/23/17273898/villanova-basketball-recruiting-josh-green-offer |title=Villanova offers 2019 guard Josh Green |publisher=VU Hoops |date=23 April 2018}} In July 2018, he received an offer to join the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]].{{cite web |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Josh-Green-Tar-Heels-Offer-Basketball-Scholarship-119856525/ |title=Tar Heels Offer Scholarship to Josh Green |publisher=247 Sports – North Carolina |date=31 July 2018}} Green was considered a top player in the 2019 recruiting class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and [[ESPN]]. On 4 October 2018, Green committed to play for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], North Carolina, Villanova, [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. Green was a consensus five-star prospect out of [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]]. In October 2018, Green signed his [[National Letter of Intent|NLI]] to the University of Arizona for basketball.{{cite web |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2018/10/04/arizona-wildcats-basketball-5-star-guard-josh-green-commits/1524889002/ |title=Josh Green joins Nico Mannion in committing to Arizona 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his second college game, Green scored 20 points as Arizona beat [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] 90–69.{{cite news |title=No. 21 Arizona routs Illinois 90–69 behind freshman trio |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169934 |access-date=19 November 2019 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=10 November 2019}} Green missed a game against [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] on 29 February due to a lower back sprain.{{cite news |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=On Sean Miller's 'conversations' with officials at UCLA, Josh Green's absence and silver linings |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/on-sean-miller-s-conversations-with-officials-at-ucla-josh/article_ccff0fe8-5b8f-11ea-84c5-e32b03bfe40c.html |access-date=1 March 2020 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |date=1 March 2020}} Green averaged 12.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.5 steals per game for the Wildcats as a freshman while shooting 36.1% from three-point range. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Josh Green entering draft after first year at Arizona |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29021904|access-date=10 April 2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=10 April 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2020–2024)=== Green was selected with the 18th pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite news |title=Mavericks select Josh Green with No. 18 pick in NBA draft |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2020/11/18/mavericks-select-josh-green-with-no-18-pick-in-nba-draft/ |access-date=18 November 2020 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]] |date=18 November 2020}} He signed his rookie scale contract with the Mavericks on 30 November 2020.{{cite news|title=With training camp around the corner, Mavs sign Green and Bey|url=https://www.mavs.com/greenbeysign/|access-date=30 November 2020|work=mavs.com|date=30 November 2020}} Green made his NBA debut on 23 December, scoring two points in a 106–102 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |title=BOOKER, BRIDGES LEAD NEW-LOOK SUNS PAST MAVERICKS 106–102 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000004 |access-date=6 February 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On 18 February 2021, Green received his first [[NBA G League]] assignment, to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]]. The Mavericks qualified for the postseason, but were eliminated in the first round by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. Green played four total minutes during the seven-game series.{{Cite web |title=STARS CARRY CLIPPERS AT MAVS AGAIN, 106–81 ROUT EVENS SERIES |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000174 |access-date=6 February 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On 19 October 2021, Mavericks picked up Green's option for another year until the 2022–23 season.{{Cite tweet|user=MavsPR|number=1450509587287773189|title=The Dallas Mavericks have extended the contract of forward Josh Green.|date=19 October 2021}} On 27 December, after a stint in health and safety protocols, Green had a career-high 10 assists in a 132–117 win against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web |title=Mavericks vs. Trail Blazers – Game Recap – December 27, 2021 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401360325 |access-date=6 April 2022 |publisher=ESPN |language=en}} On 7 January 2022, Green scored a season-high 17 points in a 130–106 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |title=Mavericks vs. Rockets – Game Recap – January 7, 2022 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401360405 |access-date=6 April 2022 |publisher=ESPN |language=en}} Two days later, he surpassed his season high by scoring 18 points in a 113–99 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |title=Bulls vs. Mavericks – Game Recap – January 9, 2022 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401360422 |access-date=6 April 2022 |publisher=ESPN |language=en}} On 21 April 2022, during the Mavericks' first round playoff series against the [[Utah Jazz]], Green recorded 12 points, three rebounds, six assists and two steals in a 126–118 game 3 win.{{Cite web |title=BRUNSON, MAVERICKS BEAT JAZZ 126–118 TO TAKE 2–1 SERIES LEAD |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100173 |access-date=6 February 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} The Mavericks won their first playoff series and reached the [[NBA Conference Finals|Western Conference Finals]], both for the first time since [[2011 NBA playoffs|2011]]. However, they fell to the eventual champions, the [[Golden State Warriors]], in five games.{{Cite web |title=WARRIORS BEAT MAVERICKS 120–110 TO RETURN TO NBA FINALS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100315 |access-date=6 February 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On 20 November 2022, Green scored 23 points, alongside two rebounds, in a 98–97 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web |title=RARE BUZZER-BEATER HELPS OUTMANNED NUGGETS BEAT MAVS 98–97 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200246 |access-date=6 February 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On 9 December, during a 106–105 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], he suffered an elbow injury.{{Cite magazine |title=Josh Green Speaks on Latest Injury Recovery Update |url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavs-josh-green-latest-injury-recovery-update |access-date=6 February 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=12 January 2023 }} He missed twenty straight games before returning to the lineup on 18 January 2023, scoring nine points in a 130–122 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |title=YOUNG, HAWKS BEAT DONCIC, MAVS 130–122 FOR 4TH STRAIGHT WIN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200670 |access-date=6 February 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On 6 February 2023, Green scored a career-high 29 points in a 124–111 win over the Utah Jazz.{{cite web|title=Josh Green steps up as Mavericks secure Kyrie Irving|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/35606013|publisher=ESPN|access-date=25 March 2023|date=6 February 2023}} On 23 October 2023, Green signed a three-year, $41 million extension with the Mavericks.{{Cite web|title=Dallas Mavericks' Josh Green Agrees To 3-Year, $41 Million Extension|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/doylerader/2023/10/23/dallas-mavericks-josh-green-agrees-to-3-year-41-million-extension/|access-date=23 October 2023|website=forbes.com}} Green helped the Mavericks reach the [[2024 NBA Finals]] where they lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|publisher=cbsnews.com|access-date=17 June 2024|date=17 June 2024}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2024–2026)=== On 6 July 2024, Green was traded by the Mavericks to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in a six-team sign and trade which also included the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Denver Nuggets]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], which became the NBA's first six-team transaction.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Josh Green, Reggie Jackson And Two Second-Round Picks In Six-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-acquire-josh-green-reggie-jackson-and-two-second-round-picks-in-six-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=6 July 2024|access-date=7 July 2024}} He made 68 appearances (67 starts) for Charlotte during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.4 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 1.6 assists.{{Cite web |title=Josh Green Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/greenjo02.html |access-date=2026-08-30 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} On 20 June 2025, Green underwent surgery to address instability in his left shoulder.{{Cite web|title=Josh Green undergoes left shoulder surgery; expected to make a full recovery|url=https://www.si.com/nba/hornets/news/josh-green-undergoes-left-shoulder-surgery-expected-to-make-a-full-recovery|access-date=2 October 2025|website=si.com|language=en}} Green made his season debut on 12 December 2025.{{Cite web |date=2025-12-13 |title=Hornets' Josh Green: Logs 17 minutes in return |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hornets-josh-green-logs-17-minutes-in-return/ |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}} ===Utah Jazz (2026–present)=== On 10 July 2026, Green, alongside [[LaMelo Ball]], was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in a four-team trade.{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Guards LaMelo Ball and Josh Green from Charlotte Hornets |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-guards-lamelo-ball-and-josh-green-from-charlotte-hornets |access-date=July 10, 2026 |publisher=[[Minnesota Timberwolves]]}} However on 29 August 2026, Green was traded again, this time to the [[Utah Jazz]] alongside cash considerations in exchange for [[John Konchar]] and [[Cody Williams]].{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Acquire Josh Green {{!}} Utah Jazz |url=https://utahjazz.com/news/utah-jazz-acquire-josh-green |access-date=2026-08-29 |website=utahjazz.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Green was named in the 24-man squad selected to represent the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian national team]] in [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Asia)|FIBA World Cup Qualifiers]] against [[Qatar men's national basketball team|Qatar]] and [[Kazakhstan men's national basketball team|Kazakhstan]] in September 2018.{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/josh-green-talks-aussie-boomers-squad-nod-looking-up-to-ben-simmons-and-dant-exum-and-getting-an-offer-from-north-carolina/news-story/f16404f8c221cd86d7075051f92592c1 |title=Josh Green talks Aussie Boomers squad nod, looking up to Ben Simmons and Dante Exum, and getting an offer from North Carolina |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=3 August 2018}} However, a torn labrum in his right shoulder prevented him from making his international debut. In January 2019, Green revealed his ambitions to represent Australia at the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Tokyo Olympics]]. On 6 February 2019, Green was named in the 23-man squad selected to represent [[Australia national under-19 basketball team|Australia's Under-19 national team]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/potential-nba-draftee-josh-green-named-in-emus-squad-20190206-p50w2s.html |title=Potential NBA draftee Josh Green named in Emus squad |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=6 February 2019}} In March 2019, Green signalled his aspiration to represent Australia at the [[2019 FIBA World Cup]].{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/exclusive-josh-green-wants-to-make-his-australian-boomers-debut-in-the-2019-fiba-world-cup/news-story/e06b157ce8cec14bdbc9f29275200a77 |title=Exclusive: Josh Green wants to make his Australian Boomers debut in the 2019 FIBA World Cup |publisher=Fox Sports Australia |date=9 March 2019}} Green made his senior debut for Australia in the first round of the 2020 Olympics against [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigeria]] and helped his country obtain their first-ever Olympic medal in men's basketball, beating [[Slovenia men's national basketball team|Slovenia]] in the bronze medal game.{{Cite news |last=Healy |first=Jon |date=7 August 2021 |title=After finishing fourth four times, the Boomers finally get on the Olympic podium
